title: Auth Orphan Cleanup Flow
purpose: Show the fragile signup flow: Supabase auth user created → profile creation attempted → if profile fails, delete auth user via admin API. Highlight the lack of DB transaction and the race window where orphan could persist if cleanup fails.
description: The signup flow in auth.service.ts has a fragile orphan prevention mechanism: (1) Frontend submits signup request with email, password, username, role. (2) Auth service creates Supabase Auth user via supabase.auth.admin.createUser or signUp. (3) On success, profile row is created in public.profiles table. (4) If profile creation FAILS (DB error, constraint violation), auth service attempts cleanup by calling supabase.auth.admin.deleteUser(authUser.id). (5) If deletion succeeds, orphan is avoided—user returns error. (6) If deletion ALSO fails, a permanent orphan is created: the auth user exists but has no profile. The user can never log in because findUserById returns null → 404 or 401. Key issues: no DB transaction wrapping both operations, race window between auth user creation and profile insert, and no background job to scan for orphans.

businessRules: Auth user creation and profile insert are NOT wrapped in a DB transaction

securityConsiderations: Cleanup requires SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY for admin.deleteUser—exposed in frontend .env
Race window: system crash between auth user creation and profile insert creates permanent orphan
No audit log of orphan creation events
Orphaned auth users count toward Supabase Auth limits
performanceConsiderations: Cleanup attempt adds one extra API call to Supabase Auth
No performance impact during happy path (majority of requests)

annotations.text: ARCHITECTURAL ISSUE: No DB transaction wraps auth user creation + profile insert. Race window exists.
WORST CASE: Permanent orphan. Auth user exists, can authenticate via Supabase, but findUserById returns null → blocked at middleware.
Requires SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY—exposed in client .env. Service key has full auth management access.
